headline: Highest risk is medium: no shared channels are documented, but the pair’s docs-only, unverified profiles leave prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways uncertain rather than impossible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or tool pipeline is documented for either agent. Agent A is a non-runnable content-writing repo and agent B is a non-runnable email-scheduling repo with no io_surfaces shown, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains, but the profiles do not support a plausible default bridge.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF either profile gains a parser that treats the other’s output as instructions, the pathway may exist.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared channels.
Do not copy outputs between them automatically.
Review any future MCP or filesystem bridge before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows a shared workspace, sensitive data classes, or outbound file-upload behavior. Agent B explicitly has network egress set to none, and agent A exposes no io surfaces or touched data classes. With only docs-only, unverified profiles, leakage is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced and either agent uploads file contents, leakage risk changes.
IF either agent begins handling sensitive data classes, reassess compliance and leakage.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Leave agent B network egress disabled.
Avoid passing raw documents between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. Agent A has no capabilities listed and agent B only shows network egress none; neither profile indicates filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write access. Because the relevant capability surface is absent, a conflict pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk may appear.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, reassess.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write permissions.
Keep both agents read-only unless needed.
Add locking before any shared mutable workflow.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where agent A’s output becomes agent B’s authoritative input, and both profiles are non-runnable docs-only repositories. Agent B is an email-scheduling category, but no action-taking authority or verification gap is shown. The interaction is therefore not evidenced, though uncertainty is higher than zero.
conditions: IF agent A’s text is later fed into agent B without verification, cascading error risk exists.
IF agent B is given authority to send emails based on A’s outputs, reassess severity.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require source citations before any downstream action.
Disable automatic action-taking from generated text.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data handling differences are documented for either agent. Agent A touches no data classes and agent B likewise lists none, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess. Because the profiles are docs-only and unverified, the safest supported finding is none rather than inferred mismatch.
conditions: IF either agent is assigned regulated data classes, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF a DPA, HIPAA, or GDPR boundary is introduced, compliance risk may change.
mitigations: Add retention and residency checks to the workflow.
Block regulated data until policies are confirmed.
